extracted.intended_audience: writers (especially those new to or interested in flash fiction)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and submitting complete short-short stories (flash fiction / microfiction) — how to shape character, language, scope, and endings to work within strict word limits and how to find markets. Targets writers aiming to produce publishable flash pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flash fiction word-count definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete stories of fewer than 1,500, 1,000, 500, or even 300 words can be classified as flash fiction; microfiction often refers to stories of fewer than 400 words; short-shorts, immediate fiction, and sudden fiction are often used for works of 500–750 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exact definitions can vary by specific market; publishers’ uses often vary just as widely as the word limits do. Use market guidelines when submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Few Characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Favor a small cast — 'three or fewer well-drawn characters' rather than many.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describing eight characters will blow your word count. You're better off with three or fewer well-drawn characters than with eight empty shells.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptions That Show Rather Than Tell
rubrics_metrics.description: Use showing, not telling, to maximize impact within limited words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paint your characters and action with small, vivid scenes. This rule is especially important in flash fiction because your goal is to maximize the impact of each passage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verbal Efficiency / Brevity
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ the verbal economy of a poet: every word must pull weight; strive for big impact in a small package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brevity is not just the soul of wit; it is damned hard work. Example: Hemingway’s six-word story ('For sale: baby shoes, never worn') evokes far more than the words say. Aim to create that kind of resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear Vision and Completeness (strong ending)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flash fiction should be a complete story with a clear beginning and a great ending — not just a striking opening line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The best flash fiction is complete. In 100 or 500 or 1,000 words, you have to get inside your reader’s head, have an intellectual and emotional impact, and stop. Know what happens to the main character, whether she has a distinctive voice, and what the climax and resolution are. Avoid leaving readers thinking, 'But what happened then?'

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit Scope / Be Realistic About What You Can Accomplish
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize the limitations of the format and focus on a few elements done well rather than trying to replicate a full-length story's breadth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can’t paint characters, places, and times as thoroughly as you might in a full-length story, but a few elements done well will meet your reader’s expectations. Be realistic about what you can accomplish in such a short piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Small, Vivid Scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure the story around compact, telling moments rather than extended exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paint your characters and action with small, vivid scenes to convey character and plot development efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markets and Submission Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Find appropriate markets and contests that accept flash fiction using resources that allow searching by genre and story length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use resources like WritersMarket.com and duotrope.com to search by genre, story length, and other factors. Flash publishing credits can count toward professional organization membership; there are specialty publications, reprint anthologies, and contests for flash fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre Flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Flash fiction can (and is) published across genres including sci-fi, fantasy, horror, and literary fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers in multiple genres embrace the format; choose markets appropriate to your story's genre rather than assuming flash is only literary.
